prompt: What is the goodwill on the acquisition of Echo?
explanation: Fair value of net assets = 800 + equipment step-up 100 + brand 150 = 1,050. Goodwill = 1,200 − 1,050 = 150.

prompt: Prepare Delta's consolidated balance sheet at 31 December N1.
modelAnswer:
Equipment: 900 + 700 + (100 − 20 additional depreciation N1) = 1,680; brand name 150 − 30 impairment = 120; goodwill 150; inventory 400; cash 300 + 100 = 400 → total 2,750.
Share capital 1,500 (Delta only; Echo's 800 eliminated with the investment); net income 200 + 150 − 20 (depreciation of the step-up) − 30 (brand impairment) = 300; liabilities 700 + 250 = 950 → total 2,750.
keyPoints: Equipment 1,680 incl. step-up net of depreciation 20

steps.title: Follow the fair value adjustments into N1
steps.why: Step-ups are only recognised in the consolidated accounts, so their depreciation/impairment is a consolidation entry that reduces group net income.
lines: Additional depreciation on the step-up: 100 / 5 = 20 → step-up 80

pitfalls: Forgetting the extra depreciation on the equipment step-up.
Eliminating Echo's N1 profit (post-acquisition = group profit).

statement: In the consolidated income statement N1, Echo's brand impairment of 30 and the additional depreciation of 20 reduce consolidated net income.
explanation: Yes. Valuation differences from the PPA follow the asset they relate to: the equipment step-up is depreciated (−20 per year), the brand is impaired (−30). Both are consolidation adjustments not visible in Echo's own statements.

prompt: What is the impairment loss at the end of N2 and the depreciation for N3?
modelAnswer: Depreciation 50,000 per year → carrying amount end N2 = 500,000 − 2 × 50,000 = 400,000. Recoverable amount = max(300,000; 320,000) = 320,000 → impairment loss 80,000 (expense) → carrying amount 320,000. Depreciation N3 = 320,000 / 8 remaining years = 40,000.

steps.title: Recoverable amount and impairment
lines: max(FV less costs to sell 300,000; value in use 320,000) = 320,000

steps.title: Depreciation N3
steps.why: The impaired amount is spread over the remaining 8 years.

prompt: What is the reversal of impairment at the end of N3 and the carrying amount after reversal?
modelAnswer: Carrying amount end N3 before reversal = 320,000 − 40,000 = 280,000. Recoverable amount 380,000. Cap: carrying amount without any impairment = 500,000 − 3 × 50,000 = 350,000. Reversal = 350,000 − 280,000 = 70,000 (income in P/L); carrying amount 350,000; depreciation from N4 = 350,000 / 7 = 50,000.

steps.title: Cap for the reversal
steps.why: IAS 36.117: after reversal the carrying amount may not exceed what it would have been without the impairment (depreciated cost).

explanation: Identified asset (specified unit), the retailer obtains substantially all economic benefits and directs how and for what purpose the unit is used; centre rules are protective restrictions.
No identified asset: the provider has a substantive right to substitute servers and directs their operation → service contract, expensed.

prompt: For the store unit (contract 3), compute the lease liability and the right-of-use asset at commencement, and the depreciation and interest of year 1.
modelAnswer: At commencement the first payment of 50,000 is paid immediately; the liability covers the two remaining payments (beginning of years 2 and 3 = end of years 1 and 2): 50,000 × 1.8334 = 91,670. ROU = 91,670 + 50,000 paid at commencement = 141,670. Year 1: depreciation 141,670 / 3 ≈ 47,223; interest 6% × 91,670 ≈ 5,500; liability end of year 1 = 97,170 (paid on the next day).

steps.title: Which payments are in the lease liability?
steps.why: Payments in ADVANCE: the first 50,000 is paid at commencement, so it is not a liability any more. The liability = PV of the two remaining payments.

steps.title: Right-of-use asset
lines: ROU = lease liability + payments made at or before commencement

steps.title: Year 1
lines: Liability end of year 1: 91,670 + 5,500 = 97,170 (paid the next day)

pitfalls: Discounting all three payments as if paid at year end.

prompt: What is Vela's EBITDA in N?
explanation: EBITDA = operating profit + depreciation & amortisation + impairment = 480 + 380 + 40 = 900. (860 forgets the goodwill impairment.)

prompt: Explain two reasons why net cash from operating activities (690) differs from EBITDA (900).
modelAnswer: 1) Income taxes paid (around 100) are deducted in operating cash flow but not in EBITDA. 2) Changes in working capital needs (e.g. higher inventories or receivables) absorb cash. Depending on the policy, interest paid may also be included in operating cash flow. EBITDA is only an approximation of operating cash.

steps.title: What EBITDA ignores
lines: 1) Income tax paid (≈ 100) – deducted in operating cash flow, not in EBITDA
2) Change in working capital needs – more inventory/receivables absorb cash
(3) Interest paid, if the company classifies it as operating)
steps.result: Taxes and working capital explain most of the gap 900 → 690

prompt: Calculate Vela's free cash flow to the firm and to equity for N (use the cash-flow definitions; ignore the tax shield on interest).
modelAnswer: FCF to the firm = operating cash flow − net capex = 690 − 410 = 280. Net increase in financial debt = borrowings 250 − repayments 150 − lease repayments 85 = +15. FCF to equity ≈ 280 + 15 − net financial expense 80 = 215 (if interest paid is not already in operating cash flow). Dividends (120) and treasury share purchases (60) are uses of FCFE, not deductions.
keyPoints: Dividends and buy-backs are uses, not deductions

steps.title: Free cash flow to the firm
lines: FCFF = operating cash flow − net capex = 690 − 410 = 280

steps.title: Free cash flow to equity
lines: FCFE = FCFF + net debt flows − interest
steps.why: (Assuming interest paid is not already inside operating cash flow.)

steps.title: What is NOT deducted
steps.why: Dividends (120) and treasury share purchases (60) are USES of FCFE – the cash given back to shareholders – not deductions.

pitfalls: Forgetting that lease repayments are debt repayments.

prompt: What is Vela's net financial debt at 31 December N, including lease liabilities?
explanation: Borrowings 1,300 + lease liabilities 420 − cash 350 = 1,370. Since IFRS 16 lease liabilities are financial debt.

prompt: Goodwill fell from 650 to 610. What explains the change, and what does it tell an analyst?
modelAnswer: Goodwill is not amortised; the income statement shows a goodwill impairment of 40, which exactly explains the decrease (650 − 40 = 610), so there were no new acquisitions. An impairment means that the recoverable amount of a CGU fell below its carrying amount – the expected cash flows of an acquired business deteriorated (overpayment or worse prospects). It cannot be reversed.
keyPoints: Signal of worse prospects of acquired business; irreversible

steps.title: Reconcile the movement
steps.why: Goodwill is not amortised. The whole decrease is explained by the impairment → no new acquisitions or disposals.

steps.title: Interpretation for an analyst
steps.why: The recoverable amount of a CGU fell below its carrying amount: an acquired business performs worse than expected (overpayment or worse prospects). The loss is non-cash and can never be reversed.
steps.result: Impairment of 40 = warning sign about past acquisitions
